Russian-backed groups are pumping out fabricated claims about Democratic candidates, AI-manipulated

Researchers say the same Russian operations now active in the U.S. midterms have also

The Justice Department has charged two former FBI employees with making false statements
to Congress in connection with the Hunter Biden investigation. NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
The two former FBI employees, Bradley Benavides and Nikki Flores, each faced a single count
of making a false statement. They were charged by criminal complaint, which means prosecutors
have not yet secured an indictment from a grand jury. Prosecutors allege that Benavides
and Flores made materially false statements to Congress in 2023 about their knowledge
of and involvement in the FBI's investigations into Hunter Biden. Both Benavides and Flores
appeared in court for an initial hearing. Attorneys for Flores said in a statement afterwards
that Flores is a patriot who is being falsely charged on the say so of politicians, not
facts. Both Flores and Benavides are due back in court Tuesday. Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
Cybercriminal theft is a major source of fraud in the federal food assistance program known
as SNAP. Now the Trump administration is proposing that all 50 states bolster the program's
security features on the cards used to buy groceries. NPR's Juliana Kim reports.
Most food assistance cards are not chip enabled, which is the standard for most debit and credit
cards today. Cards with chips are better at protecting against a form of theft known as
card skimming, where a device can steal data. States have been slow to upgrade, largely
because it's expensive. As a result, SNAP recipients have lost millions of dollars over
the years. The Food and Nutrition Administration's new proposed rule would require states to
roll out chips within a certain time frame. This change is something that the U.S. Department
of Agriculture's Inspector General, as well as Republicans and Democrats in Congress,
have advocated for. Juliana Kim, NPR News.
Severe flooding in the Four Corners region of the American Southwest has led to water
rescues and impassable roads. The flooding follows heavy rain in the desert, where Arizona,
Colorado, and New Mexico meet. More rain is in the forecast through tomorrow. Some residents
have been told to evacuate and others to stay where they are until levels drop.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Defense attorneys for the man accused of assassinating conservative activists Charlie Kirk are suggesting
a 2029 trial date and say they need years to prepare their case. Tyler Robinson has
pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder. President Trump criticized the judge prior
to the hearing and said the case should be tried within a month. New data shows the cost
of childcare continues to be a major expense for families, as NPR's Joe Hernandez reports
typical childcare payments have now surpassed household expenses like rent and medical bills.
The report out this week from the Bank of America Institute found that the national median
cost of childcare has moderated somewhat, but there are still major pressures on families
with kids. For one, the share of households paying the most for childcare has gone up,
with the number of those spending at least $2,000 per month doubling in three years.
The report also found that childcare and school-related costs last month exceeded other categories
in the consumer price index, such as housing and medical services. Some areas have seen
median payments fall. The report found that prices spiked the most in Nashville, Tennessee,
in Jacksonville, Florida, while New York City and Washington, D.C., saw the greatest declines.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar
surface in as little as two years. Administrator Jared Isaacman says the space agency is on
track to launch Artemis 3 next summer. That's a two-week mission, but by a crew of four
will serve as a docking exercise for Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos' lunar landers. That'll
